reviews.title: Not that useful
reviews.text:
After using it for many years as a local, I can say that OpenSouq might be a good pioneer in the region, but it still does not fully serve Jordanian customers very well.
It often feels easier to find properties on Facebook, since it shows real people, and you can track members in a real estate group while moderating it through admin features. Sadly, OpenSouq is full of fake accounts that don’t respond, or agents and con artists who post fake properties.
You can have better luck roaming the streets looking for properties than using the app, because, as I said, it’s full of pitfalls, and you usually end up talking to a fake seller who is actually an agent trying to lure you in.
A lot of work needs to be done on this platform. If you want to sell an item, you’re out of luck: you get no responses unless you pay, and they only list the item for 30 days. After that, you have to re-enter the entire description and upload all the pictures again—nothing is saved.
It’s a very poor experience overall
